However, Gaussian-splatting-based methods bake illumination into appearance and thus cannot jointly reconstruct scans captured under different lighting, while existing multi-illumination inverse rendering methods struggle to handle scenes whose geometry changes across captures. We present LightFuse, a 2D Gaussian inverse rendering framework that bridges this gap by extending interactive scene reconstruction with explicit material-illumination decomposition and physically based relighting. LightFuse fuses observations across states to reconstruct a shared background and movable objects. Since geometry optimized by splatting alone is ill-suited for ray-tracing-based inverse rendering, it then performs ray-tracing-oriented geometry refinement to obtain more complete and consistent surfaces. Because rearrangement leaves materials unchanged, we jointly optimize a shared set of materials across all scans under varying illumination, with differentiable one-bounce ray tracing disentangling them from the per-scan environment lighting. Experiments on novel-state relighting of synthetic scenes and novel-state synthesis of captured real scenes show that LightFuse outperforms interactive reconstruction and adapted inverse rendering baselines, improving novel-state relighting PSNR by 6.01 dB over the strongest baseline and achieving the highest PSNR on captured scenes. Project page:this https URL.
  </details>

- **[LAION-BVD: A 13-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24845)**  `arXiv:2608.24845`  
  _Andreas Hochlehnert, Marianna Nezhurina, Mehdi Cherti, Andrej Radonjic, Thaddäus Wiedemer, Christoph Schuhmann, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  We present LAION-BVD (LAION - Big Video Dataset), a large-scale open video dataset for multimodal learning, which contains 1.3B platform-specific video URLs collected from CommonCrawl. From these, we download 80M videos with a total duration of 13.5 million hours. The dataset is designed for multimodal pre-training across the video, audio, and image modalities. Using content-aware scene detection, we extract clips for which we synthetically generate video and audio captions. Models trained on these data achieve competitive performance on standard video-text and audio-text benchmarks, with consistent improvements as training or model scale increases. Additionally, we explore video frames as an alternative source of image-text data by extracting scene-changing frames. These frames exhibit a visual distribution distinct from standard web image corpora, and models trained on this dataset achieve strong image-text retrieval performance. We release LAION-BVD to the research community. It significantly expands open access to multimodal videos at an unprecedented scale.
  </details>

- **[On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24646)**  `arXiv:2608.24646`  
  _Wei Zhou, Xiongwei Zhu, Lingdong Kong, Bo Chen, Lei Zhang, Yongyuan Liang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Reinforcement learning aligns diffusion and flow models with human preferences and task objectives, yet endpoint rewards do not specify how an intermediate denoising prediction should change. We introduce DiffusionOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework that converts image-level reward guidance into explicit self-teachers for clean-output predictions at sampled on-policy queries. At each outer iteration, a frozen exponential moving average self-teacher rolls out trajectories to supply low-noise query states and clean-output anchors. Normalized local reward gradients then synthesize bounded positive and negative self-teachers around each anchor. The student policy distills these detached self-teachers under a finite update budget before an online update refreshes the self-teacher, admitting an exact single-branch variant DiffusionOPSD*. Separating self-teacher synthesis from student backpropagation removes the decoder and reward model from student backward passes and makes synthesis and realized gains separately measurable. On SD3.5-M and step-distilled Z-Image-Turbo, DiffusionOPSD and DiffusionOPSD* achieve the best held-out score across all 20 target-reward settings, winning 19 of 20 individually with gains up to 44.0% over the strongest baseline. They also deliver up to 2.57% the base-anchored gain of ReFL and up to 90% single-reward human win rates, while joint multi-reward training transfers zero-shot with up to 81% human win rates. Separately, comprehensive profiling experiments show that DiffusionOPSD and DiffusionOPSD* use up to 63% and 74% fewer GPU-hours per 100 updates than DiffusionNFT and reach baseline terminal quality up to 13.1% faster. Overall, DiffusionOPSD provides a teacher-free paradigm converting rewards into stable intermediate supervision for diffusion post-training.
  </details>

- **[AVA-Encoder: Learning to Represent Videos via Reconstruction-Driven Agentic Self-Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12313)**  `arXiv:2608.12313`  
  _Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun, Zhijing Zhang, Bingnan Li, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Agentic video creation systems remain far from cinematic-grade quality: their underlying models struggle to plan how story, characters, visuals, and sound fit together, and high-quality creation trajectories to learn such planning abilities are scarce. Finished human films embody this knowledge, but in a tightly coupled audiovisual form that agents cannot directly read or manipulate. We propose the Agentic Video "Auto-Encoder" (AVA-Encoder), which works backward from human films, turning them into agent-native video representations with reconstruction itself as the sole supervision. It encodes a film into a Film Knowledge Graph (Film KG) of structured-text nodes, typed dependency edges, and linked multimodal assets, then regenerates the film from this graph with a fixed decoder. Crucially, by distilling reconstruction residuals into textual gradients, AVA-Encoder drives a dual-loop self-evolution: an outer loop autonomously discovers a generalizable encoding strategy entirely from unlabeled videos, while an inner loop refines each video's Film KG at test time. AVA-Encoder improves reconstruction fidelity by 20.9 percentage points over the strongest baseline, and its autonomously learned strategy outperforms a human-tuned strategy using 70% fewer prompt tokens. Our representations drive three downstream breakthroughs: (1) Film KGs enable coordinated graph-based editing and (2) improve one-shot video generation across four open-source frameworks, while (3) fine-tuning agents on our reverse-engineered trajectories boosts video creation quality by 38.7%. We release the framework and a dataset of 500 Film KGs with over 27,000 creation trajectories.
  </details>

- **[Enabling Fully Integer-Only Inference for Lightweight Detection Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24981)**  `arXiv:2607.24981`  
  _Thanh Cong Le, Michal Szczepanski, Martyna Poreba_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Vision Transformer detectors now approach the accuracy of CNNs but remain difficult to deploy on NPUs and microcontrollers because key components, including deformable attention, feature fusion, and nonlinear activation functions, are not natively compatible with integer arithmetic. Existing quantized detectors either retain operators such as Softmax, GELU, and LayerNorm or focus on heavyweight backbones, leaving lightweight detection transformers without an end-to-end integer implementation. We address this gap with I-LW-DETR, the first fully integer-only lightweight DETR, in which every operation in the forward pass, including transformer nonlinearities, is executed in integer arithmetic. I-LW-DETR is built upon three key components: a scale-preserving split convolution that assigns independent activation scale to each branch of the multi-scale projector; SD-ShiftGELU, a sign-dependent GELU approximation that preserves element-wise behavior while avoiding the accuracy degradation; and a constrained Shiftmax that maintains stable Softmax normalization. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed quantization pipeline consistently produces efficient fully integer-only models across different model scales. Across all model scales, the proposed pipeline incurs only a moderate accuracy degradation while reducing the model size by approximately $3.6\times$ and the computational cost by more than one order of magnitude.
  </details>

- **[STEREOFLOW: Progressive Stereo Matching with StereoDiT and Transition Flow Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19986)**  `arXiv:2607.19986`  
  _Hao Wang, Haoran Geng, Xiaotong Yang, Jing Tang, Songlin Wei, Linlong Lang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Stereo matching is a fundamental task in 3D reconstruction. Despite remarkable advances, the prevailing paradigms formulate stereo matching as a deterministic regression problem, collapsing the multimodal distribution modeling into a single-point estimation. This formulation suffers from a regression-to-mean bias, frequently struggling with ambiguous regions. In contrast, we introduce a prior-guided generative framework that integrates deterministic matching regression and generative distribution modeling within a complementary formulation. Built upon this formulation, we introduce StereoFlow through three key components: (i) a two-stage progressive cascade matching network that progressively produces multi-resolution stereo conditions with complementary matching cues; (ii) a pixel diffusion transformer (termed StereoDiT) with a frequency-decoupled architecture for modeling correspondence ambiguity; (iii) a few-step flow matching objective (termed Transition Flow Matching) for efficient optimization. In summary, \textsc{\textbf{StereoFlow}} achieves strong geometric consistency and rich fine-grained details in ill-posed, discontinuous regions and under zero-shot generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed StereoFlow establishes multiple state-of-the-art results across benchmarks, including Scene Flow, KITTI, ETH3D, and Middlebury.
  </details>

- **[AE-UAV: An Air-to-Air Event Camera Dataset for UAV Detection and Tracking with Continuous-Time Annotations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14726)**  `arXiv:2607.14726`  
  _Zixin Jiang, Bing He, Chaoran Xiong, Zhenzhen Wang, Xin Zhao, Ling Pei_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Perceiving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from another UAV is essential for aerial avoidance, interception, and counter-UAV operations. Event cameras suit this task because of their microsecond temporal resolution and high dynamic range. However, existing event-based UAV datasets were mostly recorded by static or ground-based observers, and their targets are annotated only at fixed frame rates. We present AE-UAV, an air-to-air event camera dataset collected from a flying UAV for detection and tracking. It contains 178 sequences of event data at 1280x720 resolution covering daytime and nighttime flights under three motion geometries. A continuous-time annotation framework based on cubic B-spline interpolation provides ground-truth boxes at arbitrary timestamps and a label for every event. Hold-out experiments confirm a median interpolation error of 2.19 pixels, reducing the piecewise-constant baseline error by 74\%. We benchmark six detectors and six trackers across illumination and motion conditions. The results show that nighttime and head-on scenarios are the hardest cases for detectors. A cross-rate generalization study further shows that learned trackers lose their accuracy when the test aggregation rate differs from the training rate. The dataset will be publicly released atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[SteerFace: Debiasing Synthetic Face Generation via Adaptive Residue Perturbation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30894)**  `arXiv:2605.30894`  
  _Yuxi Mi, Qiuyang Yuan, Jianqing Xu, Yichun Zhou, Xuan Zhao, Jun Wang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  The shortage of legally compliant data for face recognition training has sparked growing interest in using synthetic data as an alternative. While recent diffusion-based methods enable the generation of photorealistic face images with strong identity adherence and data diversity, their downstream recognition performance still exhibits a significant synthetic-real gap. This paper identifies visual tendency as a previously underexplored limitation, whereby synthetic data exhibit an unrealistic prevalence of visual attributes and thus deviate from the real-data distribution. Visual tendency can be attributed to the generator's conditioning on identity embeddings, through which co-occurring residual visual cues are unintentionally absorbed into learned identity semantics. To discourage the generator from exploiting such visual cues, this paper proposes SteerFace, a simple and efficient training framework that perturbs identity embeddings by steering them toward random orthogonal directions on the embedding hypersphere. The perturbation serves as an identity-preserving regularizer that penalizes the generator's reliance on non-identity components, as supported by theoretical analysis. This paper further introduces an adaptive strategy that learns perturbation strengths with both sample-wise preference and favorable overall statistics. Extensive experiments show that SteerFace effectively mitigates visual tendency, outperforms prior methods in downstream face recognition, and generalizes well across different training datasets and generation pipelines.
  </details>

- **[Towards Anatomically Plausible Human Image Generation via Synthetic Localized Preferences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25759)**  `arXiv:2605.25759`  
  _Bao Li, Yuliang Xiu, Zhen Liu_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Large-scale text-to-image foundation models have achieved remarkable visual realism, yet generating human images with correct anatomical structures remains challenging. Existing approaches enforce anatomical constraints through part-specific modules or localized loss weighting during supervised fine-tuning on high-quality human photos, but such datasets are limited and often provide ambiguous optimization signals due to confounding factors such as lighting, pose, and background. Preference-based alignment offers an alternative, but standard Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) treats all pixels equally and therefore fails to exploit the localized nature of anatomical artifacts. To address this, we propose the framework of Alignment via Synthetic Anatomical Preference (ASAP), which constructs controlled preference pairs through a localized degradation mechanism applied to high-fidelity human images. This mechanism performs a controlled experiment on images by introducing explicit anatomical errors in targeted regions while preserving the remaining content. With this mechanism, we create the Human Anatomical Preference (HAP) dataset with over 10K curated pairs for effective anatomical alignment of text-to-image human image generative models. To better leverage the locality of these controlled preference pairs, we introduce a localized and margin-bounded variant of DPO that prioritizes optimization in targeted anatomical regions while enforcing a finite preference margin to prevent over-optimization and preserve global semantics. We further introduce HAF-Bench, a benchmark for systematic evaluation of anatomical fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ASAP consistently reduces anatomical errors across multiple foundation models while maintaining overall image quality.
  </details>

- **[FTerViT: Fully Ternary Vision Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21171)**  `arXiv:2605.21171`  
  _Szymon Ruciński, Pietro Bonazzi, Engin Türetken, Simon Narduzzi, Michele Magno, Nadim Maamari_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Ternary Vision Transformers offer substantial model compression, however state-of-the-art methods only ternarize the encoder layers, leaving patch embeddings, LayerNorm parameters, and classifier heads in full precision. In compact models targeting resource-constrained processors, such as microcontrollers, these remaining full-precision components determine the total memory footprint, severely limiting deployment efficiency and on-device feasibility. In this work, we introduce a fully ternarized Vision Transformer in which all weight matrices and normalization parameters are ternarized, while activations remain 8-bit (FTerViT). To this end, we introduce two novel operators: TernaryBitConv2d with per-channel scaling for patch embedding and TernaryLayerNorm. FTerViT is trained using knowledge distillation, followed by a lightweight quantization-aware recovery phase. On a matched DeiT-S backbone, FTerViT reaches 77.47% ImageNet-1K top-1 at 5.81 MB, +3.27 pp over TerViT. With the stronger DeiT-III-S backbone at 384x384 resolution, our ternary W2A8 model achieves 82.43% at 6.09 MB (~15x compression, -2.42 pp vs. FP32). This backbone- and resolution-advantaged result exceeds prior ternary ViTs by up to 8 pp. Finally, we demonstrate the first implementation of ternary vision transformers on a dual-core Xtensa LX7 microcontroller inside the ESP32-S3 system-on-chip. By deploying FTerViT-Small (based on DeiT-III-Small at 224x224 resolution, 5.81 MB), we achieve 79.64% ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy.
  </details>

- **[SynVA: A Modular Toolkit for Vessel Generation and Aneurysm Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17620)**  `arXiv:2605.17620`  
  _Marten J. Finck, Niklas C. Koser, Sarker M. Mahfuz, Tameem Jahangir, Jon E. Wilhelm, Daniel Behme, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Intracranial aneurysms (IAs), characterized by unpredictable growth and risk of rupture, are a major cause of stroke and can lead to life-threatening hemorrhages with high mortality and long-term disability. With aging populations, the incidence and overall burden of cerebrovascular diseases are expected to increase, highlighting the need for scalable approaches to analyze complex medical data and improve population-level understanding of these conditions. While digital twins and deep learning offer promising avenues for improving diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, their effectiveness is limited by the scarcity of large-scale, high-quality medical data and corresponding labels. We present Synthetic VAsculature (SynVA), a modular toolkit for vascular mesh generation and anatomically consistent aneurysm synthesis. SynVA combines novel flow-matching-based methods for generating healthy vessel meshes with learning-based approaches for anatomy-conditioned aneurysm mesh generation; it computes aneurysms from pre-existing vascular geometries rather than generating them in isolation. In addition, we introduce the SynVA procedural model for vascular and aneurysm synthesis based solely on physiological principles and statistical priors, which enables the generation of large-scale datasets. To this end, we release a dataset of 50,000 fully labeled mesh samples for a variety of downstream vision tasks. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations show that SynVA generates realistic vessel geometries and anatomically plausible aneurysms, with only minor trade-offs between expert-perceived realism and similarity to real aneurysms. Moreover, pretraining on SynVA data improves point-cloud segmentation and morphological parameter estimation on real data. Code will be released upon acceptance.
  </details>

- **[ArtMesh: Part-Aware Articulated Mesh Fields with Motion-Consistent Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16582)**  `arXiv:2605.16582`  
  _Sylvia Yuan, Dan Wang, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Xinrui Cui_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  We present ArtMesh, a mesh-native method for reconstructing articulated objects explicitly as connected triangle meshes with per-part rigid motion from multi-view observations in start and end states. Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines for articulated reconstruction inherit the unstructured point-based geometry of their splatting base, which provides no surface topology for reasoning about part boundaries or enforcing motion consistency along the object's connectivity. ArtMesh instead builds on a mesh-based differentiable rendering backbone, enabling part-aware dynamics to act directly on the structured topology. To make the topology compatible with articulation, we introduce part-aware restricted Delaunay remeshing, producing connected submeshes whose triangles do not cross semantic part boundaries. The dynamic mesh field then optimizes articulation using bidirectional Vertex-wise Motion Consistency on transported mesh vertices and Pixel-wise Motion Consistency on rendered images. We introduce Articulate-100, a new benchmark of 100 articulated objects spanning 16 PartNet-Mobility categories. On this benchmark, given ground-truth part masks, ArtMesh achieves the best aggregate joint-axis estimation and part-level geometric reconstruction among prior 3DGS-based pipelines, with the largest gains on objects with many movable parts.
  </details>

- **[Invaria: Learning Scale and Density Invariance in Point Clouds via Next-Resolution Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15923)**  `arXiv:2605.15923`  
  _Chun-Peng Chang, Shaoxiang Wang, Alain Pagani, Dariu Gavrila, Holger Caesar_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Modern image encoders achieve high generalization by decoupling semantic meaning from resolution, an ability yet to be fully realized in the 3D domain. We investigate the failure of 3D point cloud encoders to achieve similar generalization and find that existing models are highly sensitive to sampling resolution and scale changes, leading to significant performance degradation. This sensitivity is a major bottleneck for real-world deployment in robotics, as it suggests models overfit to specific quantization densities and object scales rather than learning invariant semantic features. To mitigate this dependency, we propose Invaria, a point cloud encoder that achieves scale and density invariance through next-resolution prediction and receptive field calibration. While our objective is not the explicit generation of high-resolution point clouds, we find that this training objective encourages the model to learn robust, structural invariants. The resulting encoder achieves significant performance gains during resolution shifts while maintaining high efficiency through a compact model size and reduced token requirements. Specifically, on ScanNet, Invaria achieves a 56.0\% higher mIoU at 3$\times$ lower resolution and a 20\% improvement when the objects scale is reduced by a factor of 3. These gains are achieved with a 45\% smaller model size and an average reduction of 40\% in input tokens.
  </details>

- **[PoseBridge: Bridging the Skeletonization Gap for Zero-Shot Skeleton-Based Action Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11497)**  `arXiv:2605.11497`  
  _Sanghyeon Lee, Jinwoo Kim, Jong Taek Lee_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition (ZSSAR) is typically treated as a skeleton-text alignment problem: encode joint-coordinate sequences, align them with language, and classify unseen actions. We argue that this alignment is often too late. Skeletons are not complete action observations, but compressed outputs of human pose estimation (HPE); by the time alignment begins, human-object interactions and pose-relative visual cues may no longer be explicit. We call this upstream semantic loss. To address it, we propose PoseBridge, an HPE-aware ZSSAR framework that bridges intermediate HPE representations to skeleton-text alignment. Rather than adding an RGB action branch or object detector, PoseBridge extracts pose-anchored semantic cues from the same HPE process that produces skeletons, then transfers them through skeleton-conditioned bridging and semantic prototype adaptation. Across NTU-RGB+D 60/120, PKU-MMD, and Kinetics-200/400, PoseBridge improves ZSSAR performance under the evaluated protocols. On the Kinetics-200/400 PURLS benchmark, which contains in-the-wild videos with diverse scenes and action contexts, PoseBridge achieves substantial gains over prior ZSSAR methods, outperforming the strongest compared baseline by 13.3-17.4 points across all eight splits. Code is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Adaptive Slicing-Assisted Hyper Inference for Enhanced Small Object Detection in High-Resolution Imagery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19233)**  `arXiv:2604.19233`  
  _Francesco Moretti, Yi Jin, Guiqin Mario_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Deep learning-based object detectors have achieved remarkable success across numerous computer vision applications, yet they continue to struggle with small object detection in high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, where dense object distributions, variable shooting angles, diminutive target sizes, and substantial inter-class variability pose formidable challenges. Existing slicing strategies that partition high-resolution images into manageable patches have demonstrated promising results for enlarging the effective receptive field of small targets; however, their reliance on fixed slice dimensions introduces significant redundant computation, inflating inference cost and undermining detection speed. In this paper, we propose \textbf{Adaptive Slicing-Assisted Hyper Inference (ASAHI)}, a novel slicing framework that shifts the paradigm from prescribing a fixed slice size to adaptively determining the optimal number of slices according to image resolution, thereby substantially mitigating redundant computation while preserving beneficial overlap between adjacent patches. ASAHI integrates three synergistic components: (1)an adaptive resolution-aware slicing algorithm that dynamically generates 6 or 12 overlapping patches based on a learned threshold, (2)a slicing-assisted fine-tuning (SAF) strategy that constructs augmented training data comprising both full-resolution and sliced image patches, and (3)a Cluster-DIoU-NMS (CDN) post-processing module that combines the geometric merging efficiency of Cluster-NMS with the center-distance-aware suppression of DIoU-NMS to achieve robust duplicate elimination in crowded scenes. Extensive experiments on VisDrone2019 and xView, demonstrate that ASAHI achieves state-of-the-art performance with 56.8% on VisDrone2019-DET-val and 22.7% on xView-test, while reducing inference time by 20-25% compared to the baseline SAHI method.
  </details>

- **[AMIF: Authorizable Medical Image Fusion Model with Built-in Authentication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24296)**  `arXiv:2603.24296`  
  _Jie Song, Jun Jia, Wei Sun, Wangqiu Zhou, Tao Tan, Guangtao Zhai_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multimodal medical image fusion integrates complementary anatomical and functional information from different imaging modalities, providing richer image representations for clinical interpretation and assisted diagnosis. High-performance medical image fusion models are typically built upon medical images with high data sensitivity and security requirements, together with carefully designed algorithmic architectures. Collectively, these constitute intellectual property of significant value. As fusion results are circulated and reused in scenarios such as cross-institutional collaboration, traceable copyright protection and controlled authorization for these medical fusion assets are becoming increasingly important. However, existing multimodal medical image fusion models typically generate unprotected results and lack built-in copyright protection and authorization mechanisms. Conventional post-processing watermarking is independent of the fusion model, making it difficult for copyright protection to become an intrinsic capability of the model itself. To address this issue, we propose AMIF, the first Authorizable Medical Image Fusion model with built-in authentication, which integrates authorization access control into the image fusion objective. For unauthorized usage, AMIF embeds explicit and visible copyright identifiers into fusion results. In contrast, high-quality fusion results are accessible upon successful key-based authentication.
  </details>

- **[Rethinking Vector Field Learning for Generative Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19218)**  `arXiv:2603.19218`  
  _Chaoyang Wang, Yaobo Liang, Boci Peng, Fan Duan, Yunhai Tong_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Taming diffusion models for generative segmentation has attracted increasing attention. While existing approaches primarily focus on architectural tweaks or training heuristics, there remains a limited understanding of the intrinsic mismatch between continuous flow matching objectives and discrete perception tasks. In this work, we revisit diffusion segmentation from the perspective of vector field learning. We identify two key limitations of the commonly used flow matching objective: gradient vanishing and trajectory traversing, which result in slow convergence and poor class separation. To tackle these issues, we propose a principled vector field reshaping strategy that augments the learned velocity field with a detached distance-aware correction term. This correction introduces both attractive and repulsive interactions, enhancing gradient magnitudes near centroids while preserving the original diffusion training framework. Furthermore, we design a computationally efficient, quasi-random centroid encoding scheme inspired by Kronecker sequences, which integrates seamlessly with an end-to-end pixel neural field framework for pixel-level semantic alignment. Extensive experiments consistently demonstrate significant improvements over vanilla flow matching approaches, substantially narrowing the performance gap between generative segmentation and strong discriminative specialists.
  </details>

- **[ABRA: Teleporting Fine-Tuned Knowledge Across Domains for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12409)**  `arXiv:2603.12409`  
  _Mattia Bernardi, Chiara Cappellino, Matteo Mosconi, Samuele Bertaina, Enver Sangineto, Angelo Porrello, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Although recent Open-Vocabulary Object Detection architectures, such as Grounding DINO, demonstrate strong zero-shot capabilities, their performance degrades significantly under domain shifts. Moreover, many domains of practical interest, such as nighttime or foggy scenes, lack large annotated datasets, preventing direct fine-tuning. In this paper, we introduce Aligned Basis Relocation for Adaptation (ABRA), a method that transfers class-specific detection knowledge from a labeled source domain to a target domain where these classes have no annotations, and no images are selected for them. ABRA decouples a detector into class-agnostic domain experts, obtained through Objectification, and class-specific residuals learned on top of them, and projects each source residual onto the singular subspaces of the target domain expert, without training. Extensive experiments across challenging domain shifts demonstrate that ABRA successfully teleports class-level specialization under multiple adverse conditions. Our code is available on GitHub.
  </details>

- **[Beyond Anatomy: Interpreting Graph-Based ASD Classification Across ABIDE Settings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02518)**  `arXiv:2603.02518`  
  _Syeda Hareem Madani, Noureen Bibi, Adam Rafiq Jeraj, Sumra Khan, Anas Zafar, Rizwan Qureshi_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Graph neural networks can classify resting-state functional MRI connectomes, but a high score on one configuration leaves open which representation choices matter and whether the result supports broader clinical use. We examine this problem through two ABIDE-I analyses. On a balanced 400-subject subset, an AAL-based graph convolutional network (73.3%), an MSDL-based configuration (84.0%), and a five-model graph attention ensemble (95.0%) report high nominal performance. However, we show that this 95.0% result, which substantially exceeds typical multi-site ABIDE benchmarks (65-70%), stems from a single site-stratified test split of 60 subjects and does not reflect out-of-distribution generalization to unseen acquisition centers. In a separate 1,035-subject analysis with different preprocessing and parcellation, BrainGAT reaches 58.26% mean accuracy, below an SVM at 69.37%. We interpret these as comparisons of complete pipelines and retain both the favorable ensemble result and the negative broader-cohort result. Analysis of the existing summaries shows that atlas substitution changes the number of possible region pairs approximately ninefold, that accuracy on 60 test subjects changes by 1.67 percentage points per prediction, and that the best accuracy and AUC belong to different broader-cohort classifiers. Regional attribution on the baseline GCN (not the 95% GAT ensemble) highlights default-mode-network features but reflects classifier reliance rather than validated clinical biomarkers. Unresolved metric aggregation and diagnosis-aware harmonization limit the findings to exploratory classification evidence.
  </details>

- **[CORAL: Correspondence Alignment for Improved Virtual Try-On](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17636)**  `arXiv:2602.17636`  
  _Jiyoung Kim, Youngjin Shin, Siyoon Jin, Dahyun Chung, Jisu Nam, Tongmin Kim, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Existing methods for Virtual Try-On (VTON) often struggle to accurately transfer garment appearance, especially in unpaired settings where accurate person-garment correspondence is required. These methods do not explicitly supervise person-garment alignment, leaving correspondence to be learned implicitly within the generation model. In this paper, we first analyze full self-attention in DiT-based architectures and show that person-to-garment query-key matching aligned with local geometric correspondence is closely related to try-on quality. Building on this insight, we introduce CORrespondence ALignment (CORAL), a DiT-based framework that explicitly aligns query-key matching with robust external correspondences. CORAL integrates two complementary components: a correspondence distillation loss that aligns reliable matches with person-to-garment attention, and an entropy minimization loss that sharpens the attention distribution. For evaluation, we further propose a VLM-based evaluation protocol to better reflect human preference. CORAL consistently improves over the baseline, enhancing both global shape transfer and local detail preservation. Extensive ablations validate our design choices.
  </details>

- **[Saliency-Aware Multi-Route Thinking: Grounding and Reasoning on Vision-Language Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16702)**  `arXiv:2602.16702`  
  _Mingjia Shi, Yinhan He, Yaochen Zhu, Cassie Dong, Jundong Li_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Vision-language (VL) agents increasingly combine extended reasoning with ex ternal visual tools. Yet long traces can drift from the image as generated text accumulates, while directly inserting tool outputs can turn one incorrect detection into a persistent premise. We ask how inference-time computation can improve reasoning without surrendering control to the tool. We propose Saliency-Aware Principle Selection (SAP), a training-free method that evolves compact reason ing principles rather than lengthening a single token trajectory. Each principle generates independent routes from the original image and prompt. A frozen ground ing tool scores whether objects cited along these routes are visually supported; agreement, diversity, and uncertainty further control drift, collapse, and overcon fidence. The tool supplies selection evidence but never writes the reasoning or answer. Across object-hallucination benchmarks, SAP consistently improves vi sually grounded prediction under a unified model and decoding budget. Broader evaluations spanning reasoning, knowledge, OCR, documents, diagrams, and real world imagery show that this gain does not come at the expense of general VL capability. Cross-architecture and model-scale experiments further demonstrate that the principle-selection mechanism transfers beyond a single backbone, while controlled ablations confirm that both multi-route exploration and evolutionary se lection are necessary. Because routes run in parallel, SAP also reduces serial latency relative to an equally long chain. Together, these results show that scaling over governed reasoning behaviors can preserve visual evidence more effectively than simply extending the chain.
  </details>

- **[Learning Image-based Tree Crown Segmentation from Enhanced Lidar-based Pseudo-labels](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13022)**  `arXiv:2602.13022`  
  _Julius Pesonen, Stefan Rua, Josef Taher, Niko Koivumäki, Xiaowei Yu, Teemu Hakala, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Mapping individual tree crowns is essential for understanding and caring for our environment by improving the accuracy of urban tree inventories and precise monitoring of forest health. However, automatically separating tree crowns in aerial imagery is challenging because of factors like complex crown textures and frequent partial overlap between neighbouring trees. We present a method to train deep learning models to segment individual tree crowns from RGB and multispectral imagery, using pseudo-labels derived from aerial laser scanning (ALS) data. We show that incorporating information from a zero-shot instance segmentation model, Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), improves model training. Our method enables training domain-specific optical image-based models without requiring manual training annotation. We trained and evaluated the models with data from an urban area in Southern Finland and compared their performance with several baselines. Our best model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 0.621 on manually delineated tree crowns in a geographically separate test area. This represents a 21% increase in mIoU over the directly evaluated SAM 2-enhanced pseudo-labels (0.513) and a 19% increase over the best image-based baseline (0.524). Incorporating SAM 2 into the pseudo-label generation process improved the best model mIoU by 9.9%, from 0.565 to 0.621, while the average mIoU across the tested models increased by 8.4%, from 0.557 to 0.604. These results highlight that automatically generated and foundation-model-enhanced pseudo-labels can provide effective domain-specific supervision for individual tree crown segmentation without manual training annotation, despite the noise in the initial ALS-based segments.
  </details>

- **[HPC: Hierarchical Point-based Latent Representation for Streaming Dynamic Gaussian Splatting Compression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00671)**  `arXiv:2602.00671`  
  _Yangzhi Ma, Bojun Liu, Wenting Liao, Dong Liu, Zhu Li, Li Li_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  While dynamic Gaussian Splatting has driven significant advances in free-viewpoint video, maintaining its rendering quality with a small memory footprint for efficient streaming transmission still presents an ongoing challenge. Existing streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting compression methods typically leverage a latent representation to drive the neural network for predicting Gaussian residuals between frames. Their core latent representations can be categorized into structured grid-based and unstructured point-based paradigms. However, the former incurs significant parameter redundancy by inevitably modeling unoccupied space, while the latter suffers from limited compactness as it fails to exploit local correlations. To relieve these limitations, we propose HPC, a novel streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting compression framework. It employs a hierarchical point-based latent representation that operates on a per-Gaussian basis to avoid parameter redundancy in unoccupied space. Guided by a tailored aggregation scheme, these latent points achieve high compactness with low spatial redundancy. To improve compression efficiency, we further undertake the first investigation to compress neural networks for streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting through mining and exploiting the inter-frame correlation of parameters. Combined with latent compression, this forms a fully end-to-end compression framework. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that HPC substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods. It achieves a storage reduction of 67% against its baseline while maintaining high reconstruction fidelity.
  </details>

- **[db-SP: Accelerating Sparse Attention for Visual Generative Models with Dual-Balanced Sequence Parallelism](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23113)**  `arXiv:2511.23113`  
  _Siqi Chen, Ke Hong, Tianchen Zhao, Ruiqi Xie, Zhenhua Zhu, Xudong Zhang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Scaling Diffusion Transformer (DiT) inference via sequence parallelism is critical for reducing latency in visual generation, but is severely hampered by workload imbalance when applied to models employing block-wise sparse attention. The imbalance stems from the inherent variation in sparsity across attention heads and the irregular distribution of dense blocks within the sparse mask, when sequence parallelism is applied along the head dimension (as in Ulysses) or the block dimension (as in Ring Attention). In this paper, we formalize a sparse imbalance ratio to quantify the imbalance, and propose db-SP, a sparsity-aware sequence parallelism technique that tackles the challenge. db-SP contains a dual-level partitioning approach that achieves near-perfect workload balance at both the head and block levels with negligible overhead. Furthermore, to handle the evolving sparsity patterns across denoising steps and layers, db-SP dynamically determines the parallel degrees for the head and block dimensions at runtime. Experimental results demonstrate that db-SP delivers an end-to-end speedup of 1.25x and an attention-specific speedup of 1.40x over state-of-the-art sequence parallel methods on average. Code is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Guiding Visual Autoregressive Models through Spectrum Weakening](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22991)**  `arXiv:2511.22991`  
  _Chaoyang Wang, Tianmeng Yang, Yunhai Tong_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Classifier-free guidance (CFG) has become a widely adopted practice for enhancing generation quality and improving condition alignment. Recent studies have explored guidance mechanisms for unconditional generation, yet these approaches remain fundamentally tied to assumptions specific to diffusion models. In this work, we propose a spectrum weakening framework for visual autoregressive (AR) models. The method is training-free and condition-free, constructing a controllable weak model in the spectral domain without architectural modifications. Specifically, we selectively retain spectral components along the channel dimension of internal representations to weaken features without requiring a complete spatial layout. We further apply spectrum renormalization to maintain feature scales during generation. Comprehensive empirical and ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of our approach, including raster-scan, random-order, and scale-wise AR, spanning discrete and continuous modeling and covering class and text-condition scenarios, demonstrating high-quality unconditional generation and strong prompt alignment for conditional generation.
  </details>

- **[Assemble the Puzzle: Cross-Agent Utility-Aware Feature Scheduling for Bandwidth-Limited Cooperative Perception](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17843)**  `arXiv:2511.17843`  
  _Chenyi Wang, Muhammad Waqar, Wujie Wen, Ming F. Li_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Cooperative perception (CP) lets connected vehicles and roadside units detect objects beyond the inherent range limitation and occlusion of single-agent systems, yet its practicality is constrained by limited Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication bandwidth. Existing methods improve bandwidth efficiency by letting collaborating agents send only selected feature cells driven by local detection confidence, serving a centralized ego agent's request. They overlook realistic communication scheduling and neglect cross-agent redundancy. We present JigsawComm, a decentralized utility-aware feature scheduling framework that learns to ``assemble the puzzle'' of multi-agent features. Choosing who sends each region requires a utility that measures what each agent's features contribute to the collaboration. JigsawComm incorporates a lightweight feature utility estimator, learned without utility labels from the cooperative model's own leave-one-agent-out counterfactuals, which aligns utilities onto a single comparable scale across agents. From one broadcast of compact utility maps, every agent ranks the observers of each cell and sends the cells it observes best to maximize coverage and, budget permitting, second best for accuracy refinement. Each agent also broadcasts its onboard detector's lightweight bounding box list, enabling an intermediate-late hybrid fusion with our feature-anchored box consensus, which synergistically enhances the final perception results with all available observations. With every transmitted byte counted, JigsawComm at 0.45 KB per vehicle outperforms all baselines on the real-world V2X-Real benchmark, and under measured C-V2X traces on CooperScene it retains 74.5 of its 79.8 AP@0.5, at least 15.5 points above every prior art baseline.
  </details>

- **[LongScape: Advancing Long-Horizon Embodied World Models with Context-Aware MoE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21790)**  `arXiv:2509.21790`  
  _Lei Jin, Yu Shang, Yiding Ma, Xin Zhang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Video-based world models hold significant potential for generating high-quality embodied manipulation data. However, current video generation methods struggle to achieve stable long-horizon generation: classical diffusion-based approaches often suffer from temporal inconsistency and visual drift over multiple rollouts, while autoregressive methods tend to compromise on visual detail. To solve this, we introduce LongScape, a hybrid framework that adaptively combines intra-chunk diffusion denoising with inter-chunk autoregressive causal generation. Our core innovation is an action-guided, variable-length chunking mechanism that partitions video based on the semantic context of robotic actions. This aligns chunk boundaries with robotic interaction events and motion dynamics, enabling the model to flexibly generate diverse dynamics. We further introduce a Context-aware Mixture-of-Experts (CMoE) framework that adaptively activates specialized experts for each chunk during generation to produce high-quality videos with coherent chunk transitions. Extensive experiments on two embodied benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation performance. Notably, LongScape maintains high generation quality and temporal consistency over 1,000-frame rollouts. When used as synthetic training data, LongScape videos lift the success rate of a downstream VLA policy by 9.8 percentage points over real-only training, outperforming augmentation with other long-video generators. Our code is available at:this https URL.
  </details>

- **[GazeVLM: Gaze-Guided Foveated Inference for Efficient Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.16476)**  `arXiv:2509.16476`  
  _Lei Wang, Jiawen Qi, Qinyu Chen_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve remarkable multimodal performance but introduce substantial computational cost due to the large number of visual tokens. Existing approaches typically rely on token pruning, sparse attention, or additional control modules, often introducing accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. This paper presents GazeVLM, a training-free framework that leverages human gaze as a natural guidance signal for efficient inference. GazeVLM allocates computation to gaze-relevant regions through a gaze-guided region-of-interest (ROI) representation and an optional two-scale design that preserves global context. We also construct GazeVLM-VQA, to the best of our knowledge, the first real-world wearable-gaze visual question answering (VQA) dataset specifically constructed for VLM inference, containing reference images, human gaze traces, and gaze-aligned question-answer pairs. Experiments on the GazeVLM-VQA benchmark demonstrate that GazeVLM improves both answer quality and efficiency across Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and Qwen3-VL-8B models. It reduces visual tokens by up to 84.2%, prefill FLOPs by up to 92.8%, and achieves up to 11.6 times prefill speedup, while improving answer-match accuracy by up to 8.6 percentage points (pp). These results show that aligning VLM computation with human visual attention provides a promising path toward efficient VLM inference. We publicly release the GazeVLM-VQA dataset (this https URL).
  </details>

- **[Delta-SVD: Efficient Compression for Personalized Text-to-Image Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16863)**  `arXiv:2508.16863`  
  _Tangyuan Zhang, Shangyu Chen, Qixiang Chen, Junyu Yan, Jingwen Ye, Jianfei Cai_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Personalizing a text-to-image diffusion model by full fine-tuning gives the strongest subject fidelity but produces a full copy of the model per subject: a thousand personalized Stable Diffusion checkpoints approach five terabytes, so storage, not compute, is what fails to scale. We present Delta-SVD, which compresses the weight change that personalization makes rather than the model. Given only a finished checkpoint and its base, it takes a truncated SVD of each layer's weight delta and keeps the few components that carry its spectral energy, selected by a per-layer energy threshold or by a global byte budget filled by water-filling, optimal for the continuous relaxation and empirically near-optimal for discrete rank allocation. Nothing is trained and no subject image is read, so the method applies to legacy and third-party checkpoints for which training-time adapters such as LoRA were never produced. The factors merge back into dense weights at load time, so serving runs at the uncompressed model's exact latency, whereas whole-model 8-bit and 4-bit quantization slow inference by 1.5-3.4 times. On the 30-subject DreamBooth benchmark, Delta-SVD matches the uncompressed model to within 0.01 DINO at 7-fold compression and keeps 98% of its fidelity at 33-fold compression. Among post-hoc baselines, only dense-delta quantization at 411 MiB matches it; below that size Delta-SVD dominates pruning, random-rank selection, and both whole-model and dense-delta quantization on the storage-quality frontier. The same holds on 84 diverse CustomConcept101 subjects, where a 9 MiB adapter reproduces the uncompressed outputs at paired DINO 0.77, and on a fully fine-tuned SD3.5-medium MMDiT, where a 531 MB adapter matches the uncompressed model to within 0.01 DINO.
  </details>

- **[Towards High-Resolution Industrial Image Anomaly Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.12931)**  `arXiv:2508.12931`  
  _Ximiao Zhang, Min Xu, Xiuzhuang Zhou_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Current anomaly detection methods primarily focus on low-resolution scenarios. For high-resolution images, conventional downsampling often misses subtle anomalies due to the loss of fine-grained discriminative information. Although recent studies have explored lightweight networks or image tiling with ensemble strategies, they still fall short of industrial requirements for both accuracy and efficiency. To address the above issues, we propose HiAD, a general framework for high-resolution anomaly detection that identifies anomalies of varying sizes under constrained computational resources. Specifically, HiAD employs a dual-branch architecture that integrates anomaly cues across different scales to comprehensively capture both subtle and large-scale anomalies. Furthermore, it incorporates a multi-resolution feature fusion module that injects multi-scale semantic context into patch-level representations, thereby suppressing ultrafine texture variations while retaining anomaly-relevant structural details. To improve adaptability and efficiency, HiAD constructs a detector pool with an adaptive strategy selection mechanism that automatically identifies the optimal detector assignment strategy for varying input data, enabling robust anomaly detection while effectively controlling computational costs. HiAD requires neither additional supervision nor auxiliary learnable parameters and can be seamlessly integrated with a wide range of anomaly detection methods. Extensive experiments are conducted on multiple high-resolution anomaly detection benchmarks, including the specifically constructed MVTec-HD, VisA-HD, and RealIAD-HD benchmarks, as well as the existing MVTec 2 benchmark. The results consistently demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of HiAD across diverse experimental settings. The code is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[VITA: Vision-to-Action Flow Matching Policy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13231)**  `arXiv:2507.13231`  
  _Dechen Gao, Boqi Zhao, Andrew Lee, Ian Chuang, Hanchu Zhou, Hang Wang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Conventional flow matching and diffusion-based policies sample via iterative denoising from standard noise distributions (e.g., Gaussian), and require conditioning modules to repeatedly incorporate visual information during the generative process, incurring substantial time and memory overhead. To reduce the complexity, we develop VITA (Vision-To-Action flow matching policy), a noise-free and conditioning-free flow matching policy learning framework that directly flows from visual representations to latent actions. Since the source of the flow is visually grounded, VITA eliminates the need for visual conditioning during generation. As expected, bridging vision and action is challenging, because actions are lower-dimensional, less structured, and sparser than visual representations; moreover, flow matching requires the source and target to have the same dimensionality. To overcome this, we introduce an action autoencoder that maps raw actions into a structured latent space aligned with visual latents, trained jointly with flow matching. To further prevent latent action space collapse during end-to-end training, we propose flow latent decoding, which anchors the latent generation process by backpropagating the action reconstruction loss through the flow matching ODE (ordinary differential equation) solving steps. We evaluate VITA on 9 simulation and 5 real-world tasks from ALOHA and Robomimic. VITA achieves 1.9x faster inference compared to conventional flow matching with conditioning modules, while outperforming or matching state-of-the-art policies. Project page:this https URL.
  </details>

- **[Fine-Grained Instruction-Guided Graph Reasoning for Vision-and-Language Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11006)**  `arXiv:2503.11006`  
  _Yaohua Liu, Binkai Ou, Xinyuan Song, Rong Fu, Amir H. Gandomi, Simon Fong_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Vision and Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to traverse complex environments by following natural language instructions, demanding accurate alignment between visual observations and linguistic guidance. To address these challenges, we propose a fine grained instruction guided graph reasoning framework (FIGR) that enhances both spatial representation and instruction understanding during navigation. Specifically, an observation graph interaction mechanism is introduced to disentangle angular and visual cues while strengthening directed edge representations through geometric embedding, enabling more reliable spatial reasoning within the navigation graph. The key detail guidance module is implemented as Adaptive Open Vocabulary Guidance (AOVG), where a contextual role parser dynamically identifies location, object, spatial relation, and other contextual cues. This design avoids exact string matching and supports previously unseen entities and compositional expressions. For multilingual instructions, a Multilingual Semantic Adapter (MSA) maps language-specific representations into a shared navigation-semantic space. By jointly integrating structured graph reasoning with instruction critical semantic cues, the proposed approach significantly improves the agent ability to follow complex navigation instructions. On the validation-unseen splits, FIGR achieves 67 SPL on R2R and 64.8 sDTW on RxR, exceeding SPENav by 1 percentage point in SPL and PRET by 2.4 points in sDTW, respectively.
  </details>

- **[Wall-to-Wall Amazon Forest Height Mapping with Planet NICFI, Aerial LiDAR, and a U-Net Regression Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.10600)**  `arXiv:2501.10600`  
  _Fabien H. Wagner, Ricardo Dalagnol, Griffin Carter, Mayumi C. M. Hirye, Shivraj Gill, Le Bienfaiteur Sagang Takougoum, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Tree canopy height is a key indicator of forest biomass, productivity, and structure, yet measuring it accurately at regional or larger scales, whether from the ground or remotely, remains challenging. The objective of this study is to generate the first complete canopy height map of the Amazon forest at $\sim$4.78 m resolution using Planet NICFI imagery and deep learning. Specifically, we (i) trained a U-Net regression model with canopy height models (CHM) derived from tropical airborne LiDAR and their corresponding Planet NICFI images to estimate canopy height, (ii) evaluated the accuracy of our map against existing global products based on Sentinel-2/1 and Maxar Vivid2 imagery, and (iii) assessed its capacity to capture small-scale canopy height changes. Tree height predictions on the validation sample had a mean absolute error of 3.68 m, with minimal systematic bias across the full range of tree heights in the Amazon forest. The main biases are a slight overestimation (up to 5 m) for heights of 5-15 m and an underestimation for most trees above 50 m. Outperforming existing global model-based canopy height products in this region, the model accurately estimated canopy heights up to 40-50 m with minimal saturation. We determined that the Amazon forest has an average canopy height of $\sim$22 m (standard deviation $\sim$5.3 m) and exhibits large-scale patterns, ranging from the tallest forests of the Guiana Shield to shorter forests along wetlands, rivers, rocky outcrops, savannas, and high elevations. Events such as logging or deforestation could be detected from changes in tree height, and the results demonstrated a first success in monitoring the height of regenerating forests. Finally, the map of the Amazon forest canopy height is displayed.
  </details>

- **[Point2SSM++: Self-Supervised Learning of Anatomical Shape Models from Point Clouds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09707)**  `arXiv:2405.09707`  
  _Jadie Adams, Mokshagna Sai Teja Karanam, Shireen Elhabian_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Correspondence-based statistical shape modeling (SSM) stands as a powerful technology for morphometric analysis in clinical research. SSM facilitates population-level characterization and quantification of anatomical shapes such as bones and organs, aiding in pathology and disease diagnostics and treatment planning. Despite its potential, SSM remains under-utilized in medical research due to the significant overhead associated with automatic construction methods, which demand complete, aligned shape surface representations. Additionally, optimization-based techniques rely on bias-inducing assumptions or templates and have prolonged inference times as the entire cohort is simultaneously optimized. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Point2SSM++, a principled, self-supervised deep learning approach that directly learns correspondence points from point cloud representations of anatomical shapes. Point2SSM++ is robust to misaligned and inconsistent input, providing SSM that accurately samples individual shape surfaces while effectively capturing population-level statistics. Furthermore, we present extensions of Point2SSM++ tailored for dynamic spatiotemporal and multi-anatomy scenarios, showcasing the broad versatility of the framework. Through extensive validation across diverse anatomies, evaluation metrics, and clinically relevant downstream tasks, we demonstrate Point2SSM++'s superiority over existing state-of-the-art deep learning models and the traditional approach. Point2SSM++ substantially enhances the feasibility of SSM generation and significantly broadens its array of potential clinical applications.
  </details>

- **[Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34935)**  `arXiv:2611.34935`  
  _Xueyang Yu, Yifan Jing, Taiming Lu, Linrong Cai, Zhipeng Cai, Yunyang Xiong, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.
  </details>

- **[Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34934)**  `arXiv:2611.34934`  
  _Charlie Griffin, Oliver Makins, Asa Cooper Stickland, Alessandro Abate, Yarin Gal, Abby D'Cruz, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  AI monitors, classifiers that flag dangerous behaviour by AI agents, are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment. We evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor as a case study and find that measured false negative rate is highly sensitive to both the method used to generate attack policies and the level of optimisation applied within that method. This rate ranged from 0.5\% to 20.8\% across optimisation levels of a single method (reinforcement learning), and from 6.4\% to 23.0\% across methods at their best observed optimisation level (optimised prompting vs.\ transcript editing). Every attack policy was developed against proxy monitors only: all reported results show attacks transferring to the held-out GPT-5.4 target monitor. Our results suggest that monitor evasion evaluations can easily mislead: an evaluation using only basic attack methods may give false confidence that a monitor is strong.The sensitivity to attack-policy choice raises a problem: interpreting any particular result as evidence about deployment performance requires justification. The transcripts produced by attack policies are proxies for the dangerous behaviour a monitor must flag in deployment. These proxies can introduce visible artefacts, such as reasoning about a ``side task'' absent from the instructions shown to the monitor, that affect monitor judgements. Given the sensitivity above, the choice of proxy can change an evaluation's conclusion. Reading these results as evidence about deployment therefore requires a separate legitimacy argument for why the proxies are informative, including any justification of conservativeness. Making convincing arguments remains an open problem.
  </details>

- **[A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34930)**  `arXiv:2611.34930`  
  _Paul Vilars, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Maria Vakalopoulou, Dimitris Samaras, Stergios Christodoulidis, Mahdi S. Hosseini_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.
  </details>

- **[Mixture-of-Loops Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34923)**  `arXiv:2611.34923`  
  _Lianghui Zhu, Shijie Wang, Xinggang Wang, Jinze Bai, Bo Wang, Xiang Bai_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available atthis https URL
  </details>

- **[Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34887)**  `arXiv:2611.34887`  
  _Cristiano Landi, Alessio Cascione, Riccardo Guidotti_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning. Over the years, a wide variety of strategies have been proposed to define split conditions within the greedy learning framework, aiming to guide instance routing and enhance predictive performance. These strategies range from axis-parallel and oblique splits based on feature values to proximity-based splits using exemplar instances and more complex hybrid approaches. However, no single method has emerged as universally superior. In this work, we present two key contributions to the construction of greedy decision trees. First, we propose a hybrid tree architecture that integrates both feature-based and case-based splits, allowing for heterogeneous splits throughout the tree. Second, we introduce a novel type of split that leverages a selective case-based approach: when a split is needed, our method searches for the most informative subset of features to define the split, effectively balancing the specificity of case-based methods with the simplicity of feature-based ones. Experiments on a diverse set of tabular datasets show that our method outperforms standard decision trees and achieves performance on par with ensemble methods, while producing shallow trees that retain or even improve predictive accuracy.
  </details>

- **[From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34858)**  `arXiv:2611.34858`  
  _Ashkan Golgoon, Giacomo Domeniconi, Samuel Atkins, Sergio Servantez, Zain Khandwala_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Autoregressive transformers trained on tokenized tabular event streams are a simple and strong baseline for predicting financial events such as fraud. Yet institutions do not act on probabilities; they act on decisions whose consequences are asymmetric and heteroscedastic: the cost of a missed high-value fraud and that of a wrongly declined small purchase are not the same. The standard bridge is post-hoc Bayes-optimal thresholding of calibrated probabilities under a cost matrix. We ask whether fine-tuning the model to the decision objective can do better. We fine-tune the same pretrained model so that its restricted softmax over label tokens (already a distribution over business actions) maximizes expected utility under an institution-specified, amount-scaled cost matrix. Because the reward is a known function of (action, outcome, amount) and the outcome is observed in the data, the expected-utility objective and its gradient are available in closed form. This is example-dependent cost-sensitive learning whose per-example loss is linear in the predicted probability, with no sampling, critics, or advantage estimation. A KL anchor to the pretrained model and an auxiliary language-modeling term preserve calibration and the generative event model. A sampled, group-normalized (GRPO-style) variant provides the extension point to trajectory-level rewards.
  </details>

- **[Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34848)**  `arXiv:2611.34848`  
  _Tingrui Huang, Yuanyuan Deng, Qingren Yao, Joaquin Vanschoren, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Songgaojun Deng_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to time series reasoning. However, current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series. This makes it unclear whether models use timestamps to connect events with observations or simply take shortcuts. To expose this ambiguity, we reformulate time series reasoning from a world-to-series projection perspective, viewing timestamps as explicit indices that connect numerical observations and external events to shared world states. We identify three structures that timestamps can make explicit: temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment. Building on this perspective, we develop a diagnostic protocol that distinguishes timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts, a distinction that accuracy-based benchmarks cannot make. Controlled interventions on 310 questions from two tasks show that high accuracy can persist when timestamps are replaced by relative offsets or removed, while breaking event-series alignment induces systematic failures. When context is pre-aligned, models barely need timestamps. When order is missing, they use dates to recall world knowledge. Without dates, they rely on correlational shortcuts and rarely notice incorrect timestamps. These findings show that high accuracy on pre-aligned, ordered inputs does not establish that a model uses timestamps to synchronize observations with the world. We release our code, model outputs, and trajectory labels atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34830)**  `arXiv:2611.34830`  
  _Simon Baur, Wojciech Samek, Jackie Ma_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. Executed actions, or decisions, taken in this manner are only as reliable as the model's predictive capabilities, and predictions in turn are only reliable within the model's experience. Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends. In this work we offer an extensive empirical study on how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty of world models. More precisely, we present a controlled comparison of post-hoc EU (last-layer Laplace and ensembles) between two dominant models of different paradigms: 1) LeWorldModel (LeWM): A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), which predicts the next embedding without a decoder, and 2) DreamerV3: A recurrent state-space model (RSSM), which reconstructs the observation from a recurrent latent state. In ten simulated visual-control environments, we follow a controlled state perturbation of the environment state through every stage of the models up to the final EU estimate. We find that the RSSM attenuates the state perturbation through two mechanisms before it reaches an estimator on the predictor feature. Its recurrent update averages over context, so a change in a single frame reaches the state at a fraction of its size and recovers only as the change persists. Its reconstruction objective weights an entity by the pixels it covers, so a small object can be lost due to the training objective. The JEPA has neither mechanism and passes the change through all stages to the uncertainty. We further show that this translates to gaps in five uncertainty related downstream tasks, from unfamiliar-state detection to uncertainty-penalised planning: the RSSM uncertainty misses deviations that its own posterior registers, whereas the JEPA uncertainty reports what its model sees.
  </details>

- **[Gradient TD($λ$) for Non-Linear Function Approximation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34826)**  `arXiv:2611.34826`  
  _Sujeet Lahane_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Temporal difference (TD) learning is central to reinforcement learning. Many methods use semi-gradient TD, which may diverge, or develop algorithms with mean-squared Bellman or TD-error objectives that are difficult to analyze. Gradient TD algorithms overcome these challenges by using projection of the value function and present convergent off-policy algorithms. However, the algorithm for $\lambda$-return was limited to linear function approximation. Here, we extend the same to non-linear function approximation, which is desirable since many strong modern function approximators are complex and non-linear. Recent works have derived similar algorithms with a generalized projected Bellman error objective. Alternatively, we continue working with the projected Bellman error.
  </details>

- **[Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34825)**  `arXiv:2611.34825`  
  _Yihang Lu, Denica Kjorvezir, Ana Gjorgjevikj, Carola Doerr, Tome Eftimov_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  LLM routing aims to choose, for each prompt, which model in a portfolio is most likely to answer correctly. This only makes sense when the benchmark contains enough prompt-specific variation for different models to be best on different inputs. On coarse-scored LLM benchmarks, however, many models often tie for the best score, and the single best model may already leave little room for improvement. We therefore propose a routeability-first audit, instantiated as RAP and RouteabilityBench, a runnable claim-verification package. The audit is retrospective: it runs once the benchmark-portfolio score matrix exists and before router comparisons are interpreted as general evidence, rather than certifying a portfolio that has not yet been evaluated. Across four benchmarks and 66 LLMs, generic routing enhancements such as larger embedding sets, dimensionality reduction, selective abstention, clustering, and stronger regressors do not consistently outperform the single best model. The clearest positive evidence is concentrated in portfolio-dependent Omni-MATH settings, while GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and IFEval show different ways in which routing can remain hard or predictor-sensitive. Our practical recommendation is that routing gains should be reported together with routeability diagnostics, tied-best analysis, portfolio construction details, and family-corrected statistical tests.
  </details>

- **[LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34821)**  `arXiv:2611.34821`  
  _Zichen Tian, Yudong Lu, Xuansheng Wu, Na Zou, Xia Hu, Guanchu Wang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache). However, the reported gains still confound parameter revisit with other design choices, e.g., network shape and residual scale. We ask, what does parameter revisit itself buy? Using matched non-revisit controls, we find that parameter revisit itself buys almost nothing. We argue that revisit only offers a freedom an MoE already has, i.e., trading experts for depth (more layers, fewer experts each) at fixed parameters. First, at matched budgets, we decompose the state-of-the-art looped recipe, with revisit last. A non-revisit control retains all the gain. Most comes from network shape, and the rest from residual scale. We prove this scale acts as a lower learning rate on revisited layers. This helps under AdamW's uneven layer step sizes, but disappears under Muon, which keeps them nearly equal. Second, beyond matched budgets, we evaluate revisit by adding compute at fixed parameters. One extra visit gains more than doubling the experts. Yet without revisit, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute obtains 90.2% of that gain under Muon. Overall, gains come from network shape, the optimizer and added compute, which a standard MoE can adopt. Accordingly, we propose LoopTitan-Base as a stronger MoE baseline. Under Muon, it matches the strongest looped recipe without revisit or residual scale. We open-source LoopTitan and release 17 pretrained models (including LoopTitan-Base and the control). Our experiment record is public as GitHub issues, with predictions pre-registered and the full exploration history kept. This is our Phase 1 technical report, laying the foundation for follow-up studies.
  </details>
